note: Starter draft — confirm with a planning engineer before relying on it. Use for projects whose main scope is structural steel (fabrication + erection).

activities.name: Shop Drawing Approval
activities.why: Shop/detailing drawings are approved before fabrication starts — omitting the gate causes rework.

activities.name: Fabrication
activities.why: Steel is fabricated to approved drawings before delivery and erection.

activities.name: Surface Treatment (Galvanising / Painting)
activities.why: Corrosion protection is applied after fabrication and before erection — frequently missed in the logic.

activities.name: Anchor Bolts & Base-Plate Setting / Grouting
activities.why: Anchor bolts and base-plate grout must be set and reach strength before any steel column is erected on them.

activities.name: Primary Steel Erection (Columns & Main Beams)
activities.why: The main frame (columns and primary beams) is erected first and gives stability for everything that follows.

activities.name: Secondary Steel, Purlins & Bracing
activities.why: Secondary steel, purlins and bracing follow the primary frame and are needed before decking/cladding.

activities.name: Metal Decking / Cladding Installation
activities.why: Roof/wall decking and cladding follow a complete, aligned and bolted steel frame.

activities.name: Bolt Torquing / Weld Inspection (NDT)
activities.why: Connections are torqued/inspected (and site welds NDT'd) before the structure is signed off.

logic_rules.reason: Fabrication must follow approved shop drawings.
Erection follows fabrication and delivery, not before.
Steel columns are erected only after anchor bolts / base plates are set and grout has gained strength.
Secondary steel, purlins and bracing follow the erected primary frame.
Decking/cladding follows a complete, aligned and bolted steel frame.

common_issues: Steel erected before base-plate grout gains strength
Decking/cladding before the frame is bolted and aligned
